# `Q-25-5` — Element bound by two components

> Two `components` entries select the same element. The first declaration keeps it; the second is ignored for that element.

## What this means

An element can host one component. When two declarations select the
same Div or Span, for example a `.card` binding and a `#first-card`
binding on the same div, Quarto warns and keeps the component declared
first. The second component still binds to any other elements it selects.

## Why this happens

- A class binding and an id binding overlap.
- Two class bindings name classes the same element carries.

## How to fix

Narrow one of the two `bind:` selectors so they select different
elements, or remove the class from the element that should get the other
component.

## Related

- The components guide (`docs/guides/authoring/components.qmd`) describes
  the `components:` key, the element contract and the runtime.
